comparison.objective: Candidate adjusts and locks an angular gripper stop; PR-2258 squares a racked wooden face frame without moving it off its marks.
comparison.physical_skill: Candidate uses coaxial tools and coordinated countertorque; PR-2258 applies opposed bimanual forces to rack a compliant four-joint frame while preventing gross sliding.
comparison.success_condition: Candidate requires a locked angle and repeatable cycles; PR-2258 requires nearly equal diagonals, closed joints, location retention and released stillness.
comparison.reason: Opposed-force coordination is generic, while the controlled mechanisms and measured outcomes are unrelated; all material rubric details are present.
